title: On-demand evidence export API for customer security questionnaires
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Large enterprise customers repeatedly ask for machine-readable CAIQ/SIG answers plus the underlying evidence artifacts (config snapshots, KMS policy exports, SOC reports). Current playbook is manual (legal ops + solutions engineer bundles) which is slow, error-prone, and doesn't scale.

Proposal: Build a secure, auditable 'evidence export' API and companion Console flow that: (1) returns a CAIQ/SIG-compliant JSON response for a given contract or workspace, (2) bundles curated supporting artifacts (logs, config exports, screenshots, signed attestations) into a time-stamped export, and (3) allows automated redaction rules and per-customer gating.

Goals: reduce manual effort for high-touch contracts by 70%, enable self-serve evidence delivery for >=30% of incoming questionnaire requests, and provide a tamper-evident artifact for customers and internal audit.

Why now: Increasing sales velocity into regulated industries; request backlog causing multi-week SLAs and lost deals. This API enables faster contract close and reduces SE time spent assembling evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API endpoint /v1/attestations/exports accepts a workspace_id and export_profile and returns a signed URL to a zipped bundle containing: CAIQ JSON, mapped evidence files, a human-readable index, and an export manifest with hashes.
2) Export respects RBAC: only users with contract_owner or security_viewer can request exports for that workspace.
3) Redaction rules can be applied: PII and secret keys are replaced with standard placeholders; redaction log included in manifest.
4) Every export creates an audit entry in Console with actor, time, export_profile, and hash.
5) Export generation telemetry (time to generate, bundle size) surfaces to Console metrics and SLO dashboards.
6) Legal & Security sign-off obtained for default export_profile and retention settings.
technical_requirements:
- Backend service: attestation-export-service (new) with queues for heavy artifact assembly; supports incremental streaming zips.
- Storage: signed export bundles saved to private S3 with pre-signed URL TTL and integrity hashes.
- Redaction engine: configurable rule set (regex, JSON key whitelists, metadata tags) pluggable into export pipeline.
- AuthZ: integrate with existing RBAC via internal auth service; require 2FA for exports containing high-sensitivity artifacts.
- Manifest signing: use platform KMS to sign export manifests; include signature and gateway verification helper.
- Privacy: ensure no plaintext customer secrets or raw keys are included; Security to provide denylist.
- Rate limits and quotas: per-organization export quotas with backoff; protect runtime from large bundle storms.
- API schema: OpenAPI spec added to repo and SDK wrappers (Python/JS) included in initial rollout.
- Observability: traces, export duration, artifact counts, and failure reasons instrumented and sent to telemetry pipeline.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (alpha/private pilot, 2 weeks): internal use only; enable for 3 pilot customers with SE-assisted flows. Gather feedback on artifact types and redaction false positives.
Phase 2 (beta, 4 weeks): enable self-serve via Console toggle for enterprise workspaces with 'export credits' limit. Add SDK wrappers and example scripts.
Phase 3 (GA): expose to all eligible Enterprise customers, document retention policies, and add automation hooks (webhook on export completion).
Communication: release notes, SE playbook, and a Confluence runbook with sample manifests and legal guidance.
Fallback: continue manual bundle process for unsupported artifact types; flag those exports in the manifest.
metrics:
- Mean time to first export (goal < 10s for small bundles).
- Median export generation time (goal < 120s).
- Percentage of questionnaire requests served by self-serve exports (goal >= 30% in Q2).
- SE hours saved per month (target: -120 hrs/month).
- Number of redaction incidents (goal: zero PII escapes).
